title: Towards Inclusive Fairness Evaluation via Eliciting Disagreement Feedback from Non-Expert Stakeholders*
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure anything in terms of faith or religion. It evaluates group fairness notions in machine learning models based on disagreement feedback from non-expert stakeholders, using sensitive attributes like race and gender in contexts like recidivism prediction and kidney allocation.
models_tested: COMPAS (Correctional Offender Management Profiling for Alternative Sanctions)
findings: This paper does not contain any findings related to religion or faith. Its findings focus on proposing a method to evaluate algorithmic fairness using binary disagreement feedback from non-experts, distinguishing between 'definite notions' (like calibration) that can be computed precisely and 'indefinite notions' (like equal opportunity) that can be bounded and estimated. These findings were validated on the COMPAS dataset with respect to race and gender.
